segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin are sharply divided: several who used it daily at full strength report severe reactions, including a ruined skin barrier, bright red peeling skin, or months to recover; others who started slowly (every other day, at night, with a heavy moisturizer) report it clears their skin well, sometimes after a rough second week.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin generally find the gel very drying, with one describing lasting barrier damage and fragility; others who paired it with a heavier moisturizer and a slow ramp-up say it worked without lasting harm.
segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin get mixed results: some say it clears hormonal breakouts quickly and effectively, while others report it stripped their skin of moisture entirely, leaving dry, flaky, red patches despite their naturally oily skin.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their late 40s and 50s, using the gel partly for anti-aging, report fewer visible wrinkles and fine lines after months of consistent, low-frequency use.

concerns.blemishes: Reports on blemishes are sharply divided: many reviewers, especially those managing hormonal or cystic acne, describe dramatic, lasting clearing after an expected 'purge' period of two to six months; but a substantial number say their acne got significantly worse and never recovered, including several who developed painful cystic acne for the first time or saw existing cystic acne worsen permanently after months of use.
concerns.dehydration: Nearly all reviewers say the gel is drying, ranging from mild dryness that a heavier moisturizer easily offsets to, for a minority, severe and lasting damage: several describe their skin as far drier, flakier and more fragile than before, with a couple reporting it took months to recover or required a dermatologist visit.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers say the gel reduces general redness and calms individual blemishes faster once past the adjustment period; others report the opposite while adjusting, describing their whole face turning bright red and peely, or new redness and irritation appearing when they start.
concerns.barrier: The clearest report on the skin barrier is negative: one reviewer with dry, sensitive, acne-prone skin says the gel completely ruined her skin barrier and needed months to recover, though others describe deliberately pairing it with a rich moisturizer specifically to protect their barrier while using it.
concerns.spots: A few reviewers say the gel has helped fade acne scarring or discoloration over time, but others report the opposite, that using the product itself left them with new scarring or hyperpigmentation once their skin reacted badly.
concerns.aging: Reviewers using it partly for anti-aging, mostly in their late 40s and 50s, report fewer visible wrinkles and fine lines after months of consistent use.

A while back, I was curious if adapelene could be used for anti-aging since it is a retinoid. Turns out, several studies have been done and have confirmed it's effective for anti-aging. I've been using it for 18 months now and have seen a decrease in wrinkles and fine lines. I have always used it in cycles. At first it was a day on and two days off. Now it's 2 days off, 1 day of an AHA, 3 days on, 1 day of AHA and then back to 2 days off everything. You just have to find what works best for your skin type. So, if you're like me and can't afford the higher priced retinoids for anti-aging, this works quite well. My picture is attached and, for reference, I'm 48. I'll be 49 in a few weeks.
